lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Can Materials Change Shape?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about materials changing shape from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about changing shape.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the four shape-change methods from Week 12.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about materials changing shape.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: How can this material change shape?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about changing shape.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about a material changing shape at home.

lessons.title: Division Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve division word problems using 2, 5 and 10.
success_criteria: I can solve a division word problem.
I can use a related times table fact.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving division word problems using a materials context (e.g. sharing clay between groups).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve division word problems, showing working.
key_questions: How many each if shared equally?
What is the related times table fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Solve division by 2, 5 and 10 with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Record division word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Make up a division word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Squashing: Testing Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to test which materials can be squashed and by how much.
success_criteria: I can test a material by squashing it.
I can compare how easily materials squash.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model testing a range of materials by squashing them, comparing results.
lessons.independent_task: Children test and compare how easily different materials squash, recording results.
resources_needed: Range of test materials (sponge, wood block, playdough, foam)

differentiation.greater_depth: Test 5+ materials and rank by squashability

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skill: comparative testing of shape-change — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Test squashing a material safely at home.

lessons.title: Writing Test Instructions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple instructions for testing a material.
success_criteria: I can write instructions using sequencing words.
I can put steps in order.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing simple instructions for testing whether a material can be bent.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 3-4 step instructions for testing a material's shape-change property.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing and sequencing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share instructions with a partner and follow them.
lessons.home_link: Write instructions for a simple task at home.

lessons.title: Measuring Stretch: Before and After
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and compare a material's length before and after stretching.
success_criteria: I can measure before stretching.
I can measure after stretching and compare.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap measuring in cm from Week 12.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring an elastic band before and after stretching, comparing the two lengths.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure and compare stretchy materials before/after stretching, recording results.

differentiation.greater_depth: Test multiple materials and compare stretch amounts

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of measuring skills to a science investigation — evidence for MATHS.MEA/SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Measure something stretchy before and after at home.

lessons.title: Bending and Twisting: Testing Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to test which materials can be bent and twisted.
success_criteria: I can test a material by bending/twisting it.
I can compare results.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap bending and twisting from Week 12.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model testing materials for bending and twisting, comparing results.
lessons.independent_task: Children test and compare materials for bending and twisting, recording results.
resources_needed: Range of test materials (wire, straw, ribbon, wood)

differentiation.greater_depth: Test 5+ materials and rank by flexibility

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skill: comparative testing of shape-change — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Test bending or twisting a material safely at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Shape-Change Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read shape-change-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read shape-change words.
I can read a sentence about testing materials.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to shape-change-themed words (e.g. 'squash', 'bend', 'twist', 'stretch').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading shape-change words over the week.

lessons.title: Recording Test Results in a Table
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to record scientific test results in a simple table.
success_criteria: I can complete a results table.
I can draw a conclusion from it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model recording test results (squash/bend/twist/stretch) in a table with tick/cross columns.
lessons.independent_task: Children record their material test results in a table and draw a simple conclusion.

differentiation.greater_depth: Draw a detailed conclusion comparing materials

lessons.assessment_notes: Record data table skill applied to a science investigation — evidence for MATHS.STAT/SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap the results tables and conclusions.
lessons.home_link: Make a simple results table for a home test.

lessons.title: Designing a Test for a New Material
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to plan a simple test for an unfamiliar material.
success_criteria: I can plan a fair test.
I can predict the result.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model planning a fair test for a new/unfamiliar material's shape-change properties.
lessons.independent_task: Children plan and predict the outcome of a test for a new material, then carry it out.
key_questions: How will you test this material?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note planning skill, a key working scientifically objective — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Plan a test for a material at home with an adult.

lessons.title: Reporting Our Material Tests
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to report test results and conclusions clearly.
success_criteria: I can report what I tested.
I can report what I found.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear scientific report.
lessons.independent_task: Children report their material test findings to a small group.

differentiation.greater_depth: Report unprompted with confidence and scientific vocabulary

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and scientific reporting skill — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Report your material test findings to your family.

lessons.title: Fractions in Testing: Half the Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply fraction knowledge to a testing context.
success_criteria: I can find half of a set of test materials.
I can group materials by property using fractions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using fractions to describe test results (e.g. 'half the materials could bend').
lessons.independent_task: Children use fraction language to describe proportions of their test results.
key_questions: What fraction of materials could be bent?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of fractions to describe real data — evidence for MATHS.N4/STAT.
lessons.home_link: Describe a fraction of something at home (e.g. half the family likes X).

lessons.title: Materials in Design and Technology
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply shape-change knowledge to a simple design task.
success_criteria: I can choose a material for its shape-change property.
I can use it in a design.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all shape-change properties tested this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss choosing materials for designs based on shape-change needs (e.g. a bendable bookmark, a stretchy wristband).
lessons.independent_task: Children design and make a simple item using a material chosen for its shape-change property.
key_questions: Why did you choose this material?
How does its shape-change property help?

differentiation.support: Adult supports material choice and construction

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of the week's material science to a design task — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Share designs made using shape-changing materials.
lessons.home_link: Find something at home designed using a shape-changing material.

lessons.title: Changing Shapes Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about materials changing shape.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about materials changing shape, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might a designer choose a stretchy material?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on this week's facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Division, Measuring, Fractions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply division, measuring and fraction skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can solve a division problem.
I can measure accurately.
I can describe fractions of results.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of division, measuring and fractions.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 17 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N3/MEA/N4.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising division facts over the weekend.

lessons.title: Changing Shapes Topic Recap and Materials Unit Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about materials and their uses/shape-changing properties.
success_criteria: I can name a way to change a material's shape.
I can explain material suitability.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the two-week materials unit (uses and shape-changing).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the unit's learning about materials.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a final 'Materials' unit display.
key_questions: What have we learned about materials?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: End of Materials unit consolidation summary for each child — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about materials this unit with your family.
